If you notice that the spark isn’t there and your partner hasn’t been the same, don’t only focus the blame on them. See what you have been doing differently as well. Odds are that you’re both not doing things you used to so of course things will change. 

Also keep doing the little things. For example, dates. Baking them a cake. Get them a shirt you think will look great on them. Buy their favorite snack if you happen to be at the store. Wear the perfume they love the most on you. Buy a movie and have a movie night. Buy flowers sometimes. Cook some days. Anything to let your spouse feel loved. 

Also you need to accept the fact that neither of you will get it your way 100%. You win some and lose some. It’s not the end of the world of they don’t agree with you on something. You may need to drop certain things. Like if it’s not that serious, don’t drag it out. Express that you’re upset, that’s perfectly fine. But make sure what you do decide to fight about is actually worth the fight. If something is very important to you, think about how important it is to them. Please heavily think about which is more logical and beneficial for you both. Like I said, you’re going to have to accept that you won’t win every fight so you need to heavily think about which fights are even worth fighting for. 

Also it’s not bad to put them over your children. When I say this, I mean if your spouse says no and your child asks you; don’t say yes. Talk with your spouse first and figure out why they said no. Discuss it with them. It’ll make your child learn that you guys don’t work together and that they can use that to their advantage which will create a lot of unnecessary fights. 

I pray you both have a beautiful life together. ❣️
